title: Sliding reserve sculptor and synthetic utilization prober for smoother burst hedging
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a sliding reserve allocator that smooths ephemeral burst allocations and a synthetic-util prober to improve utilization estimates for aggressive autoscaling. Backwards compatible; config-gated under feature flag.
description:
Motivation: We've observed short-duration microbursts that either oversubscribe warm pools or cause conservative autoscaler behavior because utilization signals are noisy at 1s windows. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a Sliding Reserve Sculptor that maintains a time-decayed reserve band per-tenant that can be partially loaned for short bursts while preserving a safety floor; (2) a Synthetic Utilization Prober that emits lightweight synthetic load samples to reconstruct a higher-fidelity utilization distribution over configurable lookback windows. Implementation is opt-in via cluster config and tenant policy flags.

Key behaviors: - Reserve decays smoothly with a configurable half-life (default 60s) to avoid cliffy deallocations. - Borrowing path allows ephemeral burst tokens up to a fraction of the decayed reserve; borrowings are recorded in an escrow ledger to prioritize repayment during quiet windows. - Prober emits controlled synthetic requests at low QPS (default 0.05 rps/tenant) with randomized timing to fill gaps and improve JV-metric estimation. The prober is rate-limited, tagged for observability, and can be disabled per-pool. - Autoscaler integration: the sliding reserve contributes a smoothed headroom estimate to the autoscaler input; the autoscaler uses the prober-augmented histogram to compute P95 and P99 utilization with less variance.

Compatibility & rollout: all changes are behind flags: cluster.feature.sliding_reserve.enabled and tenant.policy.synthetic_prober.enabled. Default in staging is enabled; disabled in GA for conservative rollout. No API schema changes to public endpoints.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-9743) - [x] Unit + integration tests for reserve decay and loan accounting - [x] End-to-end canary on staging cluster - [x] Metrics + dashboards updated - [x] Docs (internal) for ops runbook

Files changed (high level) are: a new controller package in pkg/autoscaler/reserve_sculptor.go, a light-state ledger pkg/store/escrow_ledger.go, prober implementation under pkg/telemetry/synthetic_prober.go, hooks into autoscaler/input_transform.go, test fixtures, and dashboard YAML updates. See changed_files for specifics.

Performance note: In staging with the prober enabled and default parameters, P95 latency regressions were <1% and token throughput variance reduced by ~18% across tenant-shaped workloads. Observability: new metrics reserved_capacity, reserve_loans, probe_success_ratio, prober_inflight, and reserve_decay_rate.

Risks & mitigation: - Wrong decay param could starve real throughput: mitigated by conservative defaults + kill-switch per-tenant. - Synthetic probing could add cost under extreme scale: rate-limited and aggregated per-tenant with global cap.

Requesting: review of loan accounting correctness and autoscaler integration math.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can you walk through the escrow repayment order? If multiple tenants borrow, we need deterministic tie-breaks to avoid starvation.
Maya Chen: Repayment is ordered by borrow timestamp then by tenant priority weight; added comment and a deterministic comparator in escrow_ledger.go.
Lena Morales: The prober introduces synthetic traffic — how do we ensure it doesn't bias autoscaler learning?

Maya Chen: The prober marks probe requests with a probe header and they are filtered from user-visible traces and scoring. Autoscaler buckets receive a probe-aware flag so aggregation can choose to exclude probes when desired. Added metric probe_impact_estimate.
Samir Gupta: Unit test failed when run under race detector (flaky map iteration).
Maya Chen: Fixed by switching to a sync.Map for the per-pool loan map and added a stress test; reran locally under -race.
Arjun Patel: Approve after CI green and one small doc clarifying config knobs.
ci_checks: ci/integration: failed (flaky under race) -> rerun -> passed
post_merge_notes: Feature gated. Ops: enable sliding_reserve in staging for 48h, monitor reserve_loan_rate and probe_success_ratio; if probe_success_ratio < 0.9 reduce prober qps by half. Added automation in ops playbook.
rollout_plan: Canary 6 tenants in staging -> expand to 20 tenants over 24h -> monitor SLOs -> enable in prod for 5% tenants -> ramp to 100% over 2 weeks
cost_estimate: Probing estimated to add ~0.03% CPU and 0.02% network at default rates (per-cluster). Reserve bookkeeping negligible memory increase (~1MB per 1000 tenants).
